items.title: Ontario to tackle lengthy hospital emergency room waits in Mississauga and Brampton
items.summary: Emergency departments in Mississauga and Brampton are among 26 across Ontario targeted by a new provincial initiative aimed at cutting wait times and easing pressure on hospitals. The Ontario government announced Wednesday (Oct. 7) it is spending more than $47 million over four years to launch an Emergency Department Action Team (EDAT) that will work directly with selected hospitals to identify bottlenecks, improve patient flow and find ways to get people the care they need sooner. Hospital sites in Mississauga and Brampton are included in the initiative, INSAUGA Canada has learned. William Osler Health System’s Brampton Civic Hospital and Etobicoke General Hospital are part of the project, as are Trillium Health Partners’ Credit Valley Hospital and Mississauga Hospital. The initiative comes as the province acknowledges that emergency departments are facing sustained pressure from increasing patient volumes, more serious and complex cases and growing demands on the health-care system. EDAT will work with the selected hospitals to examine how patients move through the emergency department, from their initial assessment and diagnostic testing through admission or discharge. The team will look for the factors contributing to delays, to streamline processes and getting patients through the system more efficiently. The province says the 26 hospitals were selected based on factors including emergency department volumes and the potential for improvements to benefit the greatest number of patients. Operational and performance indicators, as well as representation across different hospital types and regions, were also considered.

items.title: Mississauga neighbourhood one of cheapest for homebuyers in the Greater Toronto Area
items.summary: A Mississauga neighbourhood was one of the cheapest for homebuyers in the Greater Toronto Area last month. As the real estate market remains sluggish, homebuyers could find good deals this fall. But some neighbourhoods have bigger bargains than others. Each month, real estate platform Wahi lists neighbourhoods with the most and least expensive homes. Wahi uses the median home sale prices in GTA neighbourhoods with five or more sales to create the lists. In September, the least expensive neighbourhoods included Mississauga and Etobicoke communities, according to Wahi. North York neighbourhood Flemington Park topped the list with a median sold price of $383,000 in September. Six homes sold, and it took an average of 26 days to sell properties, according to Wahi. Woodbine in Etobicoke is second on the list with a median sold price of $402,000 in September. Five homes sold, and properties spent about 42 days on the market, according to Wahi. Mississauga’s City Centre is the only Peel Region neighbourhood on this list. The median sold price for homes here was $428,750 in September. A total of 30 homes sold, and properties spent about 34 days on the market, according to Wahi. The most expensive neighbourhoods include old Toronto communities and areas known for large properties.

items.title: Mississauga maintains highest possible credit rating from Standard & Poor
items.summary: Stable outlook reflects strong financial management, economic resilience and readiness for future growth. Standard & Poor Global Ratings (S&P), a leading provider of credit ratings, research and risk analysis, has once again awarded the City of Mississauga a AAA credit rating, the highest rating possible. This marks the 23rd consecutive year the City has received the designation, recognizing its strong financial management, responsible budgeting and ability to remain on solid financial footing while planning for growth and taking on new municipal responsibilities. The rating reflects the City’s approach to strategically reinvesting property tax dollars while continuing to maintain and invest in the infrastructure, services, programs and facilities residents rely on every day. S&P noted that Mississauga remains in a strong financial position and is well prepared for the future. The report highlights the City’s careful management of revenues and spending, even amid economic uncertainty, and ability to fund infrastructure renewal and support housing growth through a combination of reserves, responsible debt financing and funding from other levels of government. While economic uncertainty and trade-related pressures continue to affect investment across Canada, S&P highlighted Mississauga’s ongoing ability to attract business investment, particularly in manufacturing, life sciences and technology. The report highlights the City’s diversified economy, resilient property tax base and strong household incomes as key factors supporting long-term financial stability. Mississauga’s strategic location and transportation network, including Canada’s busiest airport, two national railways and five major highways, continue to strengthen its position as an important economic centre.

items.title: Mississauga Turns Park Trails Into Storybook Pages With Year-Round StoryWalk Program
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, residents can now follow illustrated pages from children's books posted along walking trails at four city parks through the StoryWalk program. Mississauga Library staff chose each book to reflect diverse, family-friendly themes, and every participating park features a different story by a Canadian author, encouraging families to visit multiple locations. The city said the program combines literacy, outdoor recreation and active living, turning a routine walk into an interactive reading adventure for people of all ages. StoryWalk trails are open year-round during regular park hours and are maintained through every season, so residents can take part at their own pace whenever they like. The city invited residents to visit a participating park, get some fresh air and watch a story unfold step by step. Officials noted that once a trail's tale ends, families can continue reading the same stories at Mississauga Library branches.

items.title: Mississauga residents back subway extension, but few confident it will actually be built
items.summary: A majority of Mississauga residents support bringing subway service to downtown, but a new survey suggests there is far less agreement over whether it should take priority over improved GO service. A survey of 1,000 Mississauga residents found 65 per cent support extending subway service to downtown Mississauga near Square One, while 20 per cent oppose the idea and 15 per cent are unsure. But when residents were asked to choose between a subway extension and all-day, two-way GO train service on the Milton line, the result was almost evenly divided. Forty-five per cent picked the subway as the better transit investment, while 44 per cent chose expanded Milton GO service. Another 11 per cent were unsure. The survey was conducted by Liaison Strategies between Oct. 2 and Oct. 4, shortly after the subway proposal was raised during the Mississauga mayoral campaign. The poll found an even bigger gap between support for the subway and confidence that it will actually be built. Only 19 per cent of respondents said they were very or somewhat confident a subway extension would eventually be constructed. Four per cent were very confident and 15 per cent somewhat confident. Meanwhile, 61 per cent said they were either not very or not at all confident the project would be built, while 20 per cent were unsure.

items.title: 49-Year-Old Mississauga Man Faces 11 Charges After Sarnia Raid Turns Up Loaded Handgun, Drugs
items.summary: According to Insauga, a 49-year-old Mississauga man is facing multiple drug and firearms charges after Sarnia police searched a home in the 1700 block of London Line on Oct. 6 and seized a loaded handgun along with an estimated $16,000 worth of drugs. The Sarnia Police Service Drug Unit carried out the search with help from the force's Intelligence Unit and Emergency Response Team. Officers seized a loaded Taurus 9mm handgun along with additional ammunition during the raid, in addition to the suspected drugs. Police have not released the accused's name, but Insauga reports he faces 11 charges in total, including possession of a prohibited firearm, possession of a firearm while prohibited, possession of ammunition while prohibited, and possession of a firearm without a licence. He is also charged with carrying a concealed weapon, carrying a weapon for a dangerous purpose, and trafficking-related offences involving cocaine and methamphetamine. Police additionally laid a charge of possession of property obtained by crime.

items.title: Kenneth Law case: Families reveal the devastating toll in 'The Poison Seller'
items.summary: Mississauga’s Kenneth Law pleaded guilty to aiding suicide after selling lethal chemicals online to people around the world. A CBC investigation linked Law to at least 147 deaths, but the real number might never be known. The Poison Seller, a documentary from The Passionate Eye, examines the investigation that left families asking why police didn't halt his operations sooner, and the CBC’s Kelda Yuen sat down with the filmmaking team behind it. If you or someone you know is struggling, help is available. In Canada, you can call or text 988 to reach the Suicide Crisis Helpline. Kids Help Phone is available at 1-800-668-6868, or by texting 686868.
